description: Composite figure of six panels spanning two modalities: engineering stress–engineering strain curves and SEM fractographs. (a) plots Stress (MPa, 0–2000) vs Strain (%, 0–80) with a black curve labelled M1-HR and a red curve M1-IA; the black curve rises steeply to a peak between the 1500 and 2000 MPa gridlines at ~15 % strain, then drops abruptly to a black square marker, while the red curve peaks below 1000 MPa and runs out to a red square marker at ~72 % strain just below the 500 MPa gridline. (d) plots Stress (MPa, 0–1200) vs Strain (%, 0–60): black M2-HR peaks near the 1000 MPa gridline at ~15 % strain, red M2-IA plateaus near 700 MPa and ends at a red square marker at ~60 % strain, ~520 MPa. Thin connector lines link each curve endpoint to its fractograph. (b) M1-HR shows labelled "Flat Facets"; (c) M1-IA shows "Dimple Rupture"; (e) M2-HR shows "River Markings"; (f) M2-IA shows "Dimple Rupture". All four SEM panels carry 10 µm scale bars. The second supplied image is a magnified reproduction of panel (d) alone. The panels together demonstrate that HR conditions give high strength with brittle cleavage fracture, whereas IA conditions give lower strength with large ductility and dimpled ductile fracture.
measured_quantities: product of strength and ductility (PSE, GPa%)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an engineering stress–strain plot with x-axis 'Strain (%)' spanning 0–80 and y-axis 'Stress (MPa)' spanning 0–2000, containing two curves labelled 'M1-HR' (black) and 'M1-IA' (red).

In (a) the M1-HR black curve peaks above the 1500 MPa gridline at roughly 15 % strain, then falls steeply and terminates at a black square marker, whereas the M1-IA red curve peaks below the 1000 MPa gridline and extends to a red square marker at about 72 % strain, below the 500 MPa gridline.

Panel (d) is an engineering stress–strain plot with x-axis 'Strain (%)' spanning 0–60 and y-axis 'Stress (MPa)' spanning 0–1200, with curves labelled 'M2-HR' (black) and 'M2-IA' (red); M2-HR peaks near the 1000 MPa gridline at ~15 % strain, while M2-IA plateaus near 700 MPa and ends at ~60 % strain near 520 MPa.
Grey connector lines tie the black square marker of each HR curve to its fractograph (b) for M1 and (e) for M2, and the red square marker of each IA curve to (c) for M1 and (f) for M2.
The SEM fractographs are annotated in yellow: 'Flat Facets' in (b), 'Dimple Rupture' in (c), 'River Markings' in (e) and 'Dimple Rupture' in (f); each of the four SEM panels has a 10 µm scale bar.

The caption states that (a) and (d) are engineering stress – engineering strain plots of HR and IA samples of M1 and M2 steel respectively, and that (b–c) and (e–f) are SEM images of fractured HR and IA samples of M1 and M2 steel.

The caption writes '(b–c) SEM images of fractured HR and JA samples', using the label 'JA' where the rest of the figure and text use 'IA' — the figure legend uses 'IA', so 'JA' appears to be a typographical error.
M1 steel in the HR condition has UTS of 1712 ± 10 MPa and total elongation of 14.8 ± 0.5 %, while in the IA condition it has 867 ± 10 MPa and 71.8 ± 0.5 %.
M2 steel in the HR condition has UTS of 1055 ± 15 MPa and total elongation of 15.4 ± 0.8 %, while in the IA condition it has 698 ± 20 MPa and 59.4 ± 0.6 %.
The IA conditions give a product of strength and ductility (PSE) of 61 GPa% for M1 and 41 GPa% for M2.

The citation attributes the high strength and poor elongation of the HR samples to martensite and the improved elongation of IA samples to retained austenite and the TRIP effect, with SFE below 18 mJ/m² for both steels.
The citation associates the flat facets and river markings of the HR fractographs with brittle cleavage fracture propagation, and the fine dimples of the IA fractographs with ductile rupture.
The second supplied image is a higher-magnification crop of panel (d) alone and contains no data beyond the M2-HR/M2-IA curve.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress (MPa, 0–2000) vs engineering strain (%, 0–80) plot with legend 'M1-HR' (black curve) and 'M1-IA' (red curve). M1-HR peaks between the 1500 and 2000 MPa gridlines at ~15 % strain and breaks abruptly (black square marker); M1-IA peaks below 1000 MPa and extends to a red square marker at ~72 % strain, below the 500 MPa gridline. Grey connector lines run from the two markers to panels (b) and (c).
SEM fractograph connected to the M1-HR curve; cleavage facets with yellow arrows and the yellow text label 'Flat Facets'; 10 µm scale bar.
SEM fractograph connected to the M1-IA curve; fine dimpled surface with yellow text label 'Dimple Rupture'; 10 µm scale bar.

Engineering stress (MPa, 0–1200) vs engineering strain (%, 0–60) plot with legend 'M2-HR' (black curve) and 'M2-IA' (red curve). M2-HR peaks near the 1000 MPa gridline at ~15 % strain (black square marker); M2-IA plateaus near 700 MPa and ends at a red square marker at ~60 % strain, ~520 MPa.
SEM fractograph connected to the M2-HR curve; cleavage ledges/plateaus annotated with yellow arrows and the yellow text label 'River Markings'; 10 µm scale bar.
SEM fractograph connected to the M2-IA curve; dense fine dimples annotated in yellow as 'Dimple Rupture'; 10 µm scale bar.
A magnified, cropped reproduction of panel (d) only — same M2-HR / M2-IA stress–strain axes and legend, plus parts of the grey connector lines at the edges. No additional data.
